summary: AskUserQuestion is answerable on the phones. On native Android the option was a TextButton whose row gave the label weight but not the description, so a long description squeezed the label to one character per line and overlapped it. Each option is now one selectable row at least 48 dp tall: the label, then the description under it, in a weighted column, with a checkbox (multi-select) or radio button (single choice) at the end, and the row carries the selected state and the role. The React Native option already stacked label and description; it gets a 48 pt minimum height and the same checkbox or radio role and checked state. Both phones now also offer the desktop's 'None of the above' free text per question: typed text replaces that question's picks, a pick clears it, and the answer sent is one rule shared by all three clients (src/shared/question-answers.ts, ported in Android QuestionSelectionReducer). An answered card shows a typed answer. React Native no longer leaves a card marked Answered when the backend refuses the answer: it reopens so the user can send it again.

automated: Android QuestionRowRenderTest (JVM, Robolectric native graphics, runs in testDebugUnitTest in about 12 s): renders the real QuestionRow at 360 and 411 dp, font scale 1.0 and 1.3, for a short label, a long label, four options, multi-select, two questions and an answered card with typed text, asserts no option label wraps to fewer than 12 characters per line, and writes PNGs to apps/android/app/build/question-shots/. The same render against origin/main reproduced the reported bug: 1 character per line in 40 of the 44 label checks.

Android QuestionRowRenderTest.tappingOptionsBuildsTheAnswerTheDesktopSends: Submit stays off until every question has an answer, typed text deselects the pick, and the action carries [[typed], [iOS, Android]] in click order.
apps/mobile jest question-item.test.tsx: 48 pt checkbox/radio options, picks sent in pick order, typed text replaces picks and a pick clears it, blank text keeps Submit off.
notExercised: Not seen on a phone or emulator. The Android renders come from Robolectric's native graphics, which uses the same Compose layout and Skia text but not a device.
React Native has no image path here: jest checks props, not pixels.

The soft keyboard over the free-text field inside the inverted feed was not exercised on either phone; Android relies on the root imePadding and Compose's bring-into-view, React Native on the screen's KeyboardAvoidingView.
